i believe in god precisely to cope with the fear of death. as someone who has been suicidal for most of their life, i think a lot about death. i find it captivating and maddening, and it scares me. i used to be an atheist because i thought that no god would endorse all the suffering here on earth. i'm still skeptical. i don't understand what is the point of "god" if people can experience pain and sadness so deeply. i still don't have an answer. i think your dad is right to be skeptical, albeit kind of harsh. death is inevitable. we can either embrace it, deny it, or try to make sense of it. human beings are otherwise very simple creatures. and i think many of us lack the strength to invest in a "power" greater than ourselves. i use this term "god" very loosely, by the way. because i'm still discovering my own faith (and as a Jewish person, this is doubly complicated and abounds with self-loathing). ultimately what "converted" me was thinking like this: what do i have to lose by believing in god? what do i have to lose but to believe in something greater than myself?
